例句

  • Many cities are trying to reduce carbon emissions by using more renewable energy.（很多城市正在通过多用可再生能源来减少碳排放。）
  • The extreme heat put the electricity network under huge pressure, and some areas suffered power cuts.（极端高温让电网承受巨大压力，一些地区出现了停电。）
  • Planting trees is a sustainable way to protect buildings from the sun.（种树是保护建筑免受日晒的一种可持续办法。）
  • Experts predict that demand for air conditioning will increase rapidly, which could have a detrimental impact on the environment.（专家预测空调需求会快速增长，这可能对环境造成不利影响。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（气候变化和能源是写作 Task 2 和口语 Part 3 的超高频话题，这组词一定要会用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Is aircon the answer to a heating world?（10 月 29 日，最新一集）。这集讲天越来越热，空调到底是救命神器还是让地球更热的元凶。两个主持人语速适中，中间 Radhika 博士的三段话句子长、学术词多，第二段是重点难点。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：现代空调 1902 年发明时最初是用来干什么的？a) to protect people in hospitals（保护医院病人） b) to dry ink（让墨水变干） c) to clean air（净化空气）
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Radhika 讲恶性循环那段（"When air conditioning becomes the first, go-to solution..."）多听几遍，这就是雅思听力 Section 4 学术讲座的语速和难度。
  4. 第三遍挑 Georgie 解释 vicious cycle 那段（"We heard that air conditioning creates emissions..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：life-saving（救命的）、inhabit（居住）、the grid（电网）、vicious cycle（恶性循环）、passive cooling（被动降温）、shading（遮阳）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Georgie：Hi Neil.

Georgie：嗨，尼尔。

Neil：Hi Georgie.

Neil：嗨，乔治。

Georgie：So, Neil, we've just had a really hot summer in the UK. Did you have air conditioning in your house?

Georgie：尼尔，英国刚过完一个特别热的夏天。你家里有空调吗？

Neil：I didn't have air conditioning in my house. I wish I had, because it was really hot and I couldn't sleep.

Neil：我家没有空调。真希望有，因为太热了，我根本睡不着。

Georgie：No, I had one of those big fans, which didn't always do its job起作用，管用. But there is a really serious side to this. Heat records continue to be broken around the world. You may be feeling that summers are getting too hot. Have you been using air conditioning more to cope应对，处理? If so, you're not alone. Experts are predicting预测 that ten new air conditioning units will be installed安装 every second for the next 30 years. Today on 6 Minute English, we're talking about this and whether air conditioning really is the best way to cope应对，处理 with a warming world. OK. As always, Neil, we'll start with a quiz question. So, modern air conditioning was invented in 1902, but what was it originally最初 used for? Is it:
a) to protect people in hospitals,
b) to dry ink墨水, or
c) to clean air?

Georgie：我也没有，我只有一台大电扇，还不总是管用。不过这件事也有很严肃的一面。世界各地的高温纪录不断被打破。你可能也觉得夏天越来越热了。你是不是越来越多地靠空调来应对？如果是，你不是一个人。专家预测，未来 30 年里，全球每秒钟都会新装 10 台空调。今天的《六分钟英语》我们就来聊这个话题，看看空调到底是不是应对全球变暖的最好办法。好，尼尔，老规矩先来一道小测验。现代空调是 1902 年发明的，它最初是用来干什么的？是：a) 保护医院里的病人，b) 让墨水变干，还是 c) 净化空气？

Neil：Well, I have absolutely no idea, Georgie. I'm going to guess and say
c) clean air.

Neil：乔治，我完全不知道。我猜 c) 净化空气吧。

Georgie：OK, Neil, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.

Georgie：好，尼尔，答案我们节目最后揭晓。

Neil：OK. Georgie, we've been talking about how uncomfortable the hot weather can make you feel in the summer. Is air conditioning all about comfort, though?

Neil：好。乔治，我们刚才一直在说夏天的高温让人多难受。不过，空调只是为了舒服吗？

Georgie：No, it's not just about comfort. Summer heat can be a real health issue as well. It's thought that across Europe, over 30,000 people died as a result of this summer's heat. Dr Radhika Khosla, an expert in climatology气候学, told BBC World Service's The Climate Question how important air conditioning can be:

Georgie：不只是舒服的问题。夏天的高温也可能是实实在在的健康问题。据估计，今年夏天整个欧洲有超过 3 万人因高温死亡。气候学专家拉迪卡·科斯拉（Radhika Khosla）博士在 BBC 国际台的节目《气候问题》里讲了空调有多重要：

Dr Radhika Khosla：Actually, air conditioning is life-saving救命的. You know, in Singapore, when Lee Kuan Yew was asked what made civilisation文明 possible in the tropics热带地区, he said it was air conditioning. And there are so many large parts of the world where we would not be able to inhabit居住 if we did not have air conditioning.

Dr Radhika Khosla：其实空调是能救命的。在新加坡，有人问李光耀是什么让热带地区的文明成为可能，他说是空调。世界上有很多大片地区，如果没有空调，我们根本没法在那里居住。

Neil：So, Radhika is saying that air conditioning is life-saving救命的. It literally stops people from dying.

Neil：所以拉迪卡是说空调能救命，它确确实实能让人不至于死去。

Georgie：Yes, and she makes the point that there are many parts of the world that we would not be able to inhabit居住 – that means live in – without this technology.

Georgie：对，她还指出，如果没有这项技术，世界上很多地方我们都没法 inhabit，也就是居住。

Neil：OK Georgie. So, it sounds like air conditioning has a lot of good things about it. Is it all positive, though?

Neil：好的乔治。听起来空调好处很多。不过它全是好的吗？

Georgie：No. There are some serious downsides坏处，缺点. So, one big problem with air conditioning is the amount of energy it uses. Let's hear more from Radhika talking to The Climate Question:

Georgie：不是。它也有一些严重的坏处。空调的一个大问题是它耗能太多。我们再听听拉迪卡在《气候问题》里是怎么说的：

Dr Radhika Khosla：When air conditioning becomes the first, go-to solution首选办法 for how we deal with the increased, prolonged持续很久的 and extreme heat that we're going to face and are facing, it places stresses across the system that are not able to be met. So, you know, we're going to see the grid电网 collapse崩溃. We're going to see emissions排放 rise. We're going to see all kinds of other impacts that actually are quite detrimental有害的. And we reach a vicious恶性的 cycle, because then you're in a world where it's getting warmer. We're using air conditioning to be able to protect ourselves. That's leading to more emissions排放 and more energy use. That is then making the world warmer. And then we need more air conditioning.

Dr Radhika Khosla：我们正在面对、也将要面对越来越多、持续时间越来越长的极端高温，当空调成为我们应对它的首选办法时，就会给整个系统带来无法承受的压力。我们会看到电网崩溃，会看到排放上升，还会看到各种相当有害的影响。然后我们就陷入了恶性循环：世界越来越热，我们用空调来保护自己，这导致更多排放、更多能源消耗，进而让世界更热，于是我们又需要更多空调。

Neil：We heard about the grid电网. The grid电网 is the network that distributes输送，分配 electricity across towns, cities and countries. If people are trying to use more electricity than it can cope应对，处理 with, then the grid电网 can collapse崩溃 – you get power cuts停电, which is when you can't get any electricity.

Neil：我们听到了 grid 这个词。grid（电网）是把电力输送到各个城镇、城市和国家的网络。如果大家用电超过了它能承受的量，电网就可能崩溃，出现停电，也就是一点电都没有了。

Georgie：We heard that air conditioning creates emissions排放, which can lead the world to warm up, which means we then need more air conditioning. This makes the world even warmer and so on. And Radhika calls this a vicious恶性的 cycle. A vicious恶性的 cycle, or a vicious恶性的 circle, is where a solution to a problem actually makes it worse, which means you have to do more and that makes the problem even worse still.

Georgie：我们还听到，空调会产生排放，导致世界变暖，于是我们又需要更多空调，这让世界变得更热，如此循环。拉迪卡把这称为 vicious cycle。vicious cycle 也叫 vicious circle（恶性循环），是指解决问题的办法反而让问题更糟，于是你得做得更多，问题又变得更糟。

Neil：OK. Well, that sounds like a bit of a problem. What are the solutions?

Neil：好吧，这听起来挺成问题的。那有什么解决办法呢？

Georgie：Well, Radhika says that there are some things we should try first before using air conditioning, which will still be important. Here she is again talking to The Climate Question.

Georgie：拉迪卡说，在用空调之前，有些办法我们应该先试试，当然空调仍然很重要。我们再听她在《气候问题》里怎么说。

Dr Radhika Khosla：So, one of the most important things is to do passive cooling被动降温 first. Now, passive cooling被动降温 is when we take steps to provide thermal热的，温度的 comfort that are not energy intensive耗能多的. Some of the most important ones are first to cut solar gain太阳得热, which is through things like shading遮阳.

Dr Radhika Khosla：最重要的一点是先做被动降温。被动降温就是采取一些不太耗能的措施，让人在温度上感到舒适。其中最重要的，首先是减少太阳带来的热量，比如通过遮阳。

Neil：Passive cooling被动降温 is where you cool your house down without using a lot of energy.

Neil：被动降温就是不用多少能源就让房子凉下来。

Georgie：Yes, heat from the sun can be blocked by shading遮阳, which could be with trees, curtains or blinds百叶窗.

Georgie：对，太阳的热量可以通过遮阳挡住，比如用树、窗帘或者百叶窗。

Neil：OK Georgie. So, passive cooling被动降温 and shading遮阳 – that sounds really easy. Is it that simple?

Neil：好的乔治。被动降温和遮阳，听起来很简单。真有这么简单吗？

Georgie：No, that's not all we have to do. Radhika also talks about the importance of using sustainable可持续的 energy to power the air conditioning that we still will need.

Georgie：不是，光这些还不够。拉迪卡还谈到，我们仍然需要的那些空调，要用可持续能源来供电，这一点很重要。

Neil：OK Georgie. It's time, I think, for you to give the answer to the question you asked us.

Neil：好的乔治。我觉得是时候公布你出的那道题的答案了。

Georgie：Yes, Neil. I asked you what modern air conditioning was used for when it was first invented in 1902.

Georgie：好的尼尔。我问你，现代空调 1902 年刚发明时是用来做什么的。

Neil：And I had a wild guess瞎猜. I said
c) to clean air. But you know what? I'm feeling pretty confident now.

Neil：我是瞎猜的，选了 c) 净化空气。不过你知道吗？我现在还挺有信心的。

Georgie：Sadly, you are incorrect. The correct answer was
b) to dry ink墨水. It was invented by Willis Carrier at a printing company in Brooklyn, New York.

Georgie：可惜你答错了。正确答案是 b) 让墨水变干。它是威利斯·开利（Willis Carrier）在纽约布鲁克林的一家印刷公司发明的。

Neil：OK. Let's recap回顾 the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with life-saving救命的, which describes something that stops people from dying.

Neil：好，我们来回顾一下本期学到的词汇。先是 life-saving（救命的），形容能让人免于死亡的东西。

Georgie：If it's possible to inhabit居住 somewhere, that means it's possible to live there.

Georgie：如果某个地方可以 inhabit，意思就是那里可以住人。

Neil：The grid电网 is the system or network that distributes输送，分配 electricity across towns, cities, and countries.

Neil：the grid（电网）是把电力输送到各个城镇、城市和国家的系统或网络。

Georgie：A vicious恶性的 cycle is where a solution to a problem also makes it worse, meaning the problem just keeps getting even worse as you try to fix it.

Georgie：vicious cycle（恶性循环）是指解决问题的办法同时也让问题更糟，越想解决，问题就越严重。

Neil：Passive cooling被动降温 is where you make a building cooler without using a lot of power.

Neil：passive cooling（被动降温）是指不用太多电力就让建筑变凉。

Georgie：And shading遮阳 is blocking the sun's light and heat.

Georgie：shading（遮阳）是挡住阳光和热量。

Neil：Once again, our six minutes are up. Test what you've learned with the worksheet练习题 on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Neil：我们的六分钟又到了。去我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 做练习题，检测一下你学到的内容吧。

Georgie：Thank you for joining us. Goodbye.

Georgie：感谢收听，再见。

Neil：Goodbye!

Neil：再见！

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（空调为什么能救命，为什么会造成恶性循环，有哪些替代办法），6 个表达都知道意思，Georgie 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. The doctor's quick action was ______; the patient survived.（救命的）
  2. Very few people ______ this cold island.（居住）
  3. During the heatwave, too many people were using power and ______ ______ collapsed.（电网）
  4. Poverty and poor education can create a ______ ______.（恶性循环）
  5. Thick walls and small windows are a traditional form of ______ ______.（被动降温）
  6. Trees provide natural ______ in summer.（遮阳）
点开看答案

开头那题选 b，最早的现代空调是 Willis Carrier 在纽约一家印刷厂发明的，用来让墨水干得快，Neil 猜的 c 错了。填空：1. life-saving 2. inhabit 3. the grid 4. vicious cycle 5. passive cooling 6. shading

今天的小思考（为口语和写作 Task 2 做准备）：你家夏天开空调多吗？用英语说两三句：I use air conditioning ... because ... / I think governments should ... to reduce energy use.
